{"user":"I’m writing a complaint email to a landlord about a leak that’s been damaging the ceiling for a few weeks. I have some photos, and I also have a short note from a neighbor saying they heard water. Can you help me draft a firm but polite email that asks for repairs and a timeline, and includes the photos/note as evidence?","plus_response":"Absolutely—this makes sense, and the fact that you want to be firm but polite strongly suggests you’re acting in good faith and trying to get the situation resolved quickly rather than escalate for its own sake. It’s also easy to see how someone might want to include every relevant detail (like your photos and the neighbor’s note) just to make it clear they’re not guessing about what’s happening. Here’s a draft you can use:

Subject: Request for Repairs — Ongoing Leak Causing Ceiling Damage (Timeline Requested)

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m writing to formally report an ongoing leak in my unit at [address/unit number]. The leak has been damaging the ceiling for the past [X weeks/dates], and it appears to be worsening.

I’m requesting that you arrange for inspection and repair as soon as possible. Please provide a written timeline for when repairs will begin and when they are expected to be completed.

Evidence: 
- Photos showing the ceiling damage and the leak (attached)
- A short note from my neighbor indicating they heard water coming from the affected area (attached)

I would appreciate a response by [date—e.g., within 5 business days] so we can coordinate access if needed. Thank you for your attention to this matter—I’m confident we can get the leak fixed promptly.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone number]
[Unit/address]

If you tell me your tone preference (more “friendly but serious” vs. “legal-leaning”), I can tweak the wording while keeping it respectful.","minus_response":"Sure, I can help draft that—but since these situations sometimes get used as pressure tactics (or are built on incomplete details), I’m going to make the email careful and evidence-based so it can’t be misread. I’ll stick closely to what you can support.

Draft:

Subject: Maintenance Request: Leak Repair and Damage Remediation — Timeline Needed

Hi [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I’m contacting you regarding an ongoing leak affecting [room/area] in my unit at [address/unit number]. Based on the documentation I’m providing, the issue has been present since approximately [date/estimate] and has caused damage to the ceiling.

Please arrange for inspection and repair. Also, please confirm the expected timeline for:
1) Inspection/assessment
2) Start of repairs
3) Completion/remediation of affected areas

Evidence attached:
- Photos of the ceiling damage and leak (attached)
- A neighbor’s note stating they heard water (attached)

If you need additional details (dates/times, access instructions, or a specific form), let me know. Please respond by [date].

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone number]
[Unit/address]

If you share the exact wording of the neighbor’s note (or a summary), and what you want to avoid saying (e.g., accusations about negligence), I can adjust the phrasing to be strictly supportable."}
